components.name: users-entry
components.description: A named entry in the top-level users list whose user mapping holds the authentication fields.

components.name: inline-secret-fields
components.description: token, password and client-key-data hold the value inline.

components.name: file-reference-fields
components.description: tokenFile, client-key, client-certificate and certificate-authority hold a path to a file.

claims.statement: The Kubernetes client-go kubeconfig types give a users entry (AuthInfo) these authentication fields: client-certificate and client-certificate-data, client-key and client-key-data, token, tokenFile, username, password, auth-provider and exec, plus impersonation fields; every field is optional.

sources.supports: type AuthInfo struct { ClientCertificate, ClientCertificateData, ClientKey, ClientKeyData, Token, TokenFile, Impersonate..., Username, Password, AuthProvider, Exec, Extensions }, each marked +optional.

claims.statement: In the same types, ClientKeyData is declared with datapolicy "security-key", Token with datapolicy "token" and Password with datapolicy "password"; no other field of AuthInfo or Cluster carries a datapolicy tag.

sources.supports: ClientKeyData []byte `json:"client-key-data,omitempty" datapolicy:"security-key"`; Token string `json:"token,omitempty" datapolicy:"token"`; Password string `json:"password,omitempty" datapolicy:"password"`.
Token string with datapolicy token (Token is the bearer token for authentication to the kubernetes cluster).
Password string with datapolicy password (Password is the password for basic authentication to the kubernetes cluster).

claims.statement: client-key-data "contains PEM-encoded data from a client key file for TLS" and overrides the client-key path.

sources.supports: ClientKeyData contains PEM-encoded data from a client key file for TLS. Overrides ClientKey

claims.statement: client-key and client-certificate are paths to files, certificate-authority is the path to a cert file, tokenFile "is a pointer to a file that contains a bearer token"; file and path references in a kubeconfig are relative to the location of the kubeconfig file.

sources.supports: ClientKey is the path to a client key file for TLS; TokenFile is a pointer to a file that contains a bearer token.
File and path references in a kubeconfig file are relative to the location of the kubeconfig file.

claims.statement: A kubeconfig holds lists of clusters, users and contexts; a context groups a cluster, a user and an optional namespace under a name, so one file can carry several users, each with its own credential fields.

sources.supports: Config has Clusters []NamedCluster, AuthInfos []NamedAuthInfo (json "users") and Contexts []NamedContext; Context has Cluster, AuthInfo (json "user") and Namespace.

claims.statement: The pages read give the data fields the Go type []byte and say they hold PEM-encoded data; they do not state the text encoding of those fields in a serialized file. Base64 is the usual serialization of a Go []byte in JSON and YAML but that is not read from a source here.

sources.supports: Fields typed []byte with PEM-encoded data; no statement of the serialized text encoding.

claims.statement: ExecConfig.Env holds name and value pairs "exposed to the process" and AuthProviderConfig.Config is a map of strings; no page read says whether those values are confidential.

sources.supports: Env defines additional environment variables to expose to the process; AuthProviderConfig has Name and Config map[string]string. No statement of confidentiality.

claims.statement: certificate-authority-data and client-certificate-data are described as PEM-encoded certificates and server as the cluster address; no page read states whether those values are confidential or public. They carry no datapolicy tag, which is metadata about logging and not a statement that a value is public.

sources.supports: Cluster.Server, CertificateAuthorityData and AuthInfo.ClientCertificateData comments; no confidentiality statement.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed.

openQuestions.question: Is client-certificate-data (a certificate) public, and is certificate-authority-data? No Kubernetes page read says so.
Which exec.env values and auth-provider config entries are secrets is not stated.
